title: Sprint 2, task 2: Never make anything up
where: Real AI products check the AI's words before a customer sees them. This check is why customers can trust AskMate.
next: Go back to the portal. Your checks are running.

steps.title: When the AI makes something up
steps.body:
A real AI writes nice sentences, but sometimes it adds things that are not true: a discount nobody offered, or a product HomeShine never sold. A customer who believes it comes to the shop and is let down.
Your rule from Sprint 1 still holds: code decides the facts. Now code also checks the AI's sentence: every price and every product code in it must be one of the facts. If not, the sentence is never shown, and AskMate uses its own.
You write that check in safety.py. answer.py already calls it on every reply.

steps.title: Predict first
steps.body:
PRICE in safety.py is a pattern that matches a price. findall gives every match in a text. What does this print?
PRICE.findall("Only ₹12,400 today")
steps.run:
from safety import PRICE
print(PRICE.findall('Only ₹12,400 today'))
steps.explain: findall gives the digits as text, with the comma still in. You turn each one into a whole number yourself.

steps.title: Find every price in a sentence
steps.body: The problem. To check prices, you first need every price a sentence mentions, as numbers.
steps.ask: Make prices_in give every price in a text, as whole numbers.
steps.gives: a list of numbers: [12400, 9900]. An empty list when there is no price.
approach: PRICE.findall(text) already gives every price's digits as text, like ['12,400', '9,900'].
Each one still has its commas. Remove them with replace(",", "").
Turn each one into a number with int().
Return them as a list. A list comprehension does all of this in one line.
steps.done: every row of the Try it table is green.
hints: Look at what findall gave in your prediction. What is still between you and a number?
Loop over PRICE.findall(text). For each one, remove the commas, then int() it.
Nearly there:  return [int(p.replace(",", "")) for p in PRICE.findall(____)]

answer.why: findall finds every price, however it is written, and gives its digits as text. Removing the commas lets int() turn each one into a number you can compare.

steps.well_done: Every price in a sentence is a number now.

args: Sorry, we do not sell that.

steps.title: Is this sentence safe to show?
steps.body: The problem. A sentence can mention a price or a product that is not in the facts. That sentence must never reach a customer.
steps.ask: Make is_safe say True only when every price and every product code in the text is one of the facts.
steps.gets: the AI's sentence, and the facts AskMate gave it, like [{"code": "OPC 186", "name": "Glanza", "price": "₹12,400"}]
approach: Collect the allowed prices: run prices_in on each fact's price, and put them all in one set.
Collect the allowed codes: a set of each fact's code.
codes_in_text(text) already gives the codes the sentence mentions.
Safe means: the sentence's prices are all allowed, and its codes are all allowed. Two sets and <= again, like in task 1.
steps.done: every row of the Try it table is green.
hints: Make two sets of what is allowed, from the facts. Then check the sentence against them.
allowed_prices: a set, then update() it with prices_in(f["price"]) for each fact. allowed_codes: {f["code"] for f in facts}.
Nearly there:  return set(prices_in(text)) <= allowed_prices and set(codes_in_text(text)) <= ____

answer.why: The facts are the only truth. Anything the sentence says that is not in them, a price or a product, was made up. <= between sets is True when everything on the left is also on the right.

steps.well_done: No made-up price or product can reach a customer now.

cases.show: no prices or codes at all
args: Sorry, HomeShine does not sell that.
Did you mean New Smile (₹1,250) or New Gold (₹1,350)?
